er-`admitted` prep-queue shape and same `faff-awaiting-spec-review` label, surfaced under its own line so a slow review is never presented as an outage.
- **`declined`** (additive, issue-keyed): `{reason, at, recorded_at}` per routed-out or claimed-by-peer candidate, written only by `faff run-ledger record-declined`; the runner pre-check's `faff drain-filter` skips an issue declined here and unchanged since `at`.
- **`landing_resumable`** (informational, additive — top-level `[issue-id]` array) — the ids of issues whose `faff-graft` landing loop returned the resumable hold token: its 25-minute landing-time budget elapsed while the PR was still open and not yet terminal-green (still waiting on CI, mid-`BEHIND`-rebase-churn, or a settling merge state) — genuinely recoverable, not a defect and not a human escalation. These issues **land in `outcomes` as `pr-open`** — the exact same bucket the hard-parked 3-cycle `pr-open-for-human` outcome also uses, so this array is the disambiguator: a `pr-open` id present here is a resumable hold (a later drain re-enters the landing loop, no rebuild), a `pr-open` id absent here is a genuine human handoff. Orthogonal annotation, not a bucket — **outside** the `runcheck` completeness invariant, no ledger migration needed. Append the id here **only** on the resumable-hold token — never on the hard-park. Drives the distinct run-summary subsection `## Awaiting landing (resumable)` so a resumable hold is never presented as a human-blocking PR. Empty on a run with no such hold.
- **`post_merge_verification_failures`** (`[{issue, pr, merge_sha, command}]`) **/ `post_merge_verification_unverified`** (`[issue-id]`) (both informational, additive, top-level arrays) — populated **at reconciliation** (step 11.6, below) by reading each shipped issue's `<run-dir>/<issue>/post-merge-verification.json` artifact, never written by the build subagent itself. `verified-fail` (merged main HEAD failed its own declared `UNIT` rung on re-run — a tracker comment + `source: "post-merge"` discovered-scope entry were already filed per-issue at Step 10, this array is only the run-level roll-up) lands in `_failures`; `unverified` (no `UNIT` rung declared, or a worktree/fetch/execution error — a genuinely unprovable verdict, not a defect, so nothing else was filed) lands in `_unverified`. These issues **still land in `outcomes` as `shipped`** — mirrors `review_adversarial_skipped` exactly: orthogonal annotations, not a bucket, **outside** the `runcheck` completeness invariant, no ledger migration needed. Drive the distinct run-summary subsections `## Shipped (post-merge verification failed)` / `## Shipped (post-merge verification unverified)` so a merge that broke — or couldn't be checked — on re-run is never presented as an undifferentiated auto-merge. Empty on a run with no post-merge failure/unverified.
- **`budget`** — the resolved `BudgetEnvelope` plus the `tokens_at_start` baseline, written **once at run start** (alongside the owner stamp): `{ envelope: {ceilings, at_ceiling, price_per_mtok, pricing}, tokens_at_start }`. `faff budget check` reads it each between-units checkpoint; `tokens_at_start` is the run-start transcript-sum so the token dimension counts *this run's* spend, not whole-session history. Absent ⇒ no budget set (every check returns `breached: []`). Informational to `runcheck` — outside the completeness invariant. The envelope's `pricing` field names which rule governs `budget.cost` — always `"map"` (priced per-model × per-class from the built-in map) for a freshly-minted run; `"flat"` only survives on a **legacy** ledger minted before the `budget.price_per_mtok` scalar was removed (its own recorded price/pricing is honoured verbatim so an in-flight run's ceiling never changes mid-run — see `faff budget check`'s docs). When events are token-tagged, this block additionally carries `tokens_at_start_by_class` (the run-start four-class baseline that seeds the per-event checkpoint) and an advancing `tokens_at_last_event` (the last tagged event's cumulative); both are additive telemetry state the CLI maintains — `budget check` still gates on the scalar `tokens_at_start` total, unchanged. A best-effort `tokens_at_start_by_model_class` (per-model baseline, seeded at mint by a lights-out run) additionally sharpens `budget.cost`'s per-model delta under map pricing; its absence (a pre-change ledger) degrades safely to a pro-rated estimate, warned rather than silently wrong.
- **`stop_reason`** (informational, additive) — the run's `Stop reason` token (one of `queue-drained` / `all-remaining-parked` / `budget-hit(<dims>)` / `budget-escalated(<dims>)` / `sentry-abort` / `converged/both-dry` / `non-convergence` / `product-incomplete` / `governance-admit-failed`) recorded **machine-readably** at orchestrator exit, so `faff disposition` can classify a run-level escalation (`budget-escalated(...)` / `non-convergence` / `product-incomplete` / `sentry-abort`) after the container dies — the same value the summary's `Stop reason:` line carries. **Written by `faff run close`** in the same locked edit as the owner close (by `faff run open` for `governance-admit-failed`); a `run checkpoint` `fail-closed` exit closes with `sentry-abort`. **Outside** the `runcheck` completeness invariant and **absent on legacy ledgers** (tolerated: `faff disposition`'s run-level escalation detection then degrades to the abort marker + per-issue outcome classification only). It never gates anything itself — it is the durable form of a signal the summary already carries in prose.
- **`owner`** — the liveness contract that lets the Stop hook tell an *in-flight* run apart from an *abandoned* one. Without it, a parallel session's hook can't distinguish "an orchestrator is actively draining this" from "this queue was deferred", and it false-blocks the unrelated session (see _Stop hook_ below).
